thread:
Maya Patel: FYI — NorAm Utilities wants an on‑prem air‑gapped POC in GovCloud. Their checklist: offline license activation, HSM/KMS support without outbound internet, SBOM + signed bundles, preferred upgrade cadence = quarterly (they say max 90 days), and minimal physical media transfers. Also asked for reserved pricing + support rates. Security questionnaire attached: <https://files.redwood.com/nau/sec-q-2026.pdf>

Ethan Liu: quick clarifying q's — what target HW (A100 v4, H100, or CPU only)? do they expect a jumpbox/jumpserver for bundle staging? and do they have an on‑site HSM with PKCS#11 or a managed appliance?

Maya Patel: they've confirmed A100 v4 on-prem racks, HSM is a Thales Luna (PKCS#11), and they prefer a jumpbox that we can stage signed bundles to. They want to avoid shipping multiple USBs if possible.

Samir Khan: Feasible. We can do signed delta bundles + offline activation via a signed activation file. High level flow: 1) we produce a signed bundle tarball, 2) they push to jumpbox, 3) run bootstrap which validates signature against our public key, 4) offline activation uses an activation.json signed by our licensing service. We support PKCS#11 HSM for local key operations.

Samir Khan: Example offline activation command (run on jumpbox):
```bash
redwood-bootstrap --bundle /mnt/bundles/redwood-2026-03-01.tar.gz \
  --activation /mnt/activation/nau-activation.sig 
  --hsm-module /usr/lib/libpkcs11.so --hsm-slot 0
```
This verifies bundle signature and writes local license + sealed keys to the HSM.

Julie Park: Security notes: we'll need to provide SBOM + signed SBOM attestations, CVE policy for the POC, and a timeline for pen testing before GA. For the quarterly patch ask — we can commit to 90‑day optional patch windows but need an exception process for critical CVEs (fast patch). Cert rotation can be done offline via a signed rotation package; recommend 180 days by default but ok to align to 90 if customer requires it (ops overhead increases).

Ethan Liu: On upgrades: to minimize physical transfers we suggest delta updates (signed binary diffs). For image signing we use our current artifact signer (we'll provide vendor public key to them). We can support a single jumpbox workflow where ops pulls signed bundles from their internal registry and runs the bootstrap. If they want completely offline activation (no outbound), we'll deliver an activation file signed by Redwood's license service team — customer will upload it to jumpbox.

DeployBot: Artifact uploaded: <https://artifacts.redwood.com/offline/bundles/redwood-offline-sample-2026-03.tar.gz> (signed). SHA256: 3f7e...1b9c

Maya Patel: Good. Customer also asked about pricing: reserved 1yr on‑prem support + on‑call for patch windows. Can someone draft a conservative SOW + 1yr pricing (include airgap packaging fee and extra engineering time for activation automation)? Prefer ballpark today so I can push numbers to procurement.

Ethan Liu: I'll draft SOW with two options: standard (quarterly deltas + remote support during maintenance windows) and managed (we provide jumpbox automation + 24/7 on‑call for first 90 days). Rough ballpark: standard = reserved support + $X/mo per rack (will populate exact numbers after PM approval).

Samir Khan: Also flagging enterprise blocker: offline license activation requires us to keep an internal process for generating signed activation files (manual step today). If they need fully automated timed renewals, we need a funded engineering task (~2 sprints) to build certificate vending tooling for HSM-backed offline renewals. Call this out in SOW.

Julie Park: I'll prepare the security appendix (SBOM format, signing key rotation, pen test scope). Need NAU's SOC/IR contacts and expected audit windows.

Maya Patel: Great — can we do a 30m sync with NorAm Infra + Security tomorrow 10am ET? I'll send invite once SOW draft and security appendix are ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
